read:pbl.summary:
I mapped OpenMAIC's project-based learning (PBL v2). It works as two layers.

1. A planner makes a frozen design: one call to the model, which code then validates and fills in.
2. A runtime runs that design with three model agents (Instructor, Evaluator, Simulator) over a code state machine.

The structure is worth porting as patterns, rewritten in our code with MIT credit. Three parts must not come over:
- the readiness gate, which is a model score;
- the proficiency engine, which is fed by model scores;
- the UI.

**How a project is structured** (packages/@openmaic/dsl/src/pbl.ts:3-149; lib/pbl/v2/types.ts:47-554)
- **Project:** title, description (the outcome), learningObjective, gains (3-5 things the learner gains), proficiency tier, language, exactly one Instructor role, milestones, and an optional `scenario` for role-play.
- **Milestone:** title, description, briefing (what the Instructor says to open it), completionCriteria, debrief (what it says to close it). An optional `synthesisCheck.coreConcept` goes on 1-2 stages, and code normalizes this. Status is locked, active or completed.
- **Microtask:** title, a description that is the "done" contract, 1-3 hints that guide and never solve, and a status.
  - Role-play beats add four fields: a hidden `successWhen`, a private `characterObjective`, `skillFocus` and `learnerBrief`.
- **Rubrics:** there is no rubric object. "Done" is written into each microtask's description. The planner classifies each task as convergent, gradable-open (must state what separates strong from weak) or open-reflective, and names its delivery form: artifact, argument or performance (planner-single-call-system.md:84-92).
- **Deliverables:** text, file or link submissions (types.ts:105-124).

**Generation**
- The outline stage emits `pblConfig`: at most one per course, 15-30 minutes, with an optional `scenarioRoleplay` (requirements-to-outlines/system.md:201-227).
- The single-call planner runs first: prompt → JSON → structural validation → one repair retry with the gaps listed → ids, status and order assigned in code. A tool loop is the fallback (scene-generator.ts:1075-1157; planner-single-call.ts:173-578).
- The ordinary prompt has 16 hard rules and a self-check (planner-single-call-system.md:48-104). The role-play prompt fixes the stage order (prep → roleplay → wrapup), allows exactly one character, and forbids spoilers (planner-scenario-single-call-system.md:5-75).

**Agent guidance**
- The Instructor's system prompt is built from blocks in a fixed order (instructor.ts:803-876). It has three phases: greeting, setup, instructing.
- It has only two tools: `record_observation` and `adjust_difficulty` (instructor.ts:1422-1483).
- It uses a hint ladder from L0 ("why") to L3 ("the literal answer"). Code decides whether the answer may be released yet, per tier (instructor.ts:419-492; tier-guidance.ts:40-90).
- Its teaching rules include no false either/or questions, at most one closing question, and "bind first, ask second" (instructor-base-rules.md:63-234).
- The Evaluator writes a task score from 0 to 100, and a score of 60 or more unlocks the Done button (evaluator-task.md:30-38; task-completion.ts:18-26; submission.tsx:531-560). It also writes star ratings for each milestone and a final report.

**How it runs across sessions**
- The server is stateless: the client posts the whole project on every turn and applies the patches that come back (app/api/pbl/v2/instructor/route.ts:4-14).
- When a lesson is saved, the learner's progress is stripped out and only the design template is kept (document-persistence.ts:14-49; learner-state.ts:126-178).
- On load, progress is rebuilt from a store of records: ordered by sequence number, duplicates removed, with resets and snapshots handled (fold.ts:323-382; hydration.ts:234-328).
- Re-entry reopens the active task, and the Instructor speaks first (progress.ts:75-186; open-task/route.ts).
- A finished milestone waits for an explicit Continue tap, and a finished task waits for a Done tap. Nothing advances on its own (progress.ts:463-812).
- Older chat is compressed in code, with no model call (instructor-memory.ts:13-29).
- The design target is still one sitting of 15-45 minutes (planner-single-call-system.md:58). Coming back later is resumption, not a planned multi-day project.

**Mapping to K-9 at-home projects with a grown-up**
- Our current project scene is only `{title, brief, steps}` with checkboxes held in memory. Nothing is saved or recorded (apps/web/src/components/stage/scenes.tsx:280-322).
- Grow it, and keep the 238 catalogue project scenes working by lifting each into a single stage in code:
  - milestone → a stage, one stage per sitting, with "Next time" tied to the existing planner `project` kind (planner/plan.ts:83-84);
  - briefing and debrief → read aloud through the theater's code script, never a greeting;
  - microtask → a step, with optional code checks;
  - submissions → a photo kept on the device, typed words, or "told the tutor";
  - the Instructor → our one live tutor, through a project block in the tutor prompt;
  - the grown-up → a real human role: a card per stage with materials, safety and how to help, plus a sign-off that needs the existing grown-up gate (lib/store.ts:40).
- Replace the Evaluator gate:
  - convergent steps are checked by code, which is the only evidence;
  - open and reflective steps are completed by a learner tap or a grown-up tap, recorded as activity, never mastery;
  - AI feedback is an ordinary live tutor turn, labelled, with no score or stars.
- The theater spec's §5.3 lists `pbl/*` under "never comes over" (spec line 347). It needs an explicit amendment.
- Role-play (the Simulator) belongs behind the same button as the multi-agent classroom.

risks: The core of OpenMAIC's project loop is model-graded: a task score of 60 or more unlocks Done (task-completion.ts:18-26; submission.tsx:531-560; evaluator-task.md:30-38). Porting it as-is breaks AGENTS.md rule 8 and theater spec §13.4. It has to be replaced (code checks, or learner and grown-up taps), not adapted, and the milestone stars and final 'what you learned' report are invented metrics under rule 1.

The proficiency engine is fed by model scores and by observations the model writes (dynamic-signals.ts:163; instructor.ts:1466), and it reads profile bio (proficiency.ts:297). Porting it would create a second, hidden learner model beside the mastery law.

The theater spec §5.3 (line 347) says `pbl/*` never comes over, and check-forbidden bans @openmaic imports. Without an explicit spec amendment, porting looks like a violation and invites copying the routes, which reach the OAuth adapter through lib/server/resolve-model.

Prompts are built for adults in one sitting: 15-45 minutes, external IDEs and Tableau, Chinese and coding examples, a left/center/right workspace (planner-single-call-system.md:58; instructor-base-rules.md:26-49). They need a rewrite for K-9 multi-day home projects, not a translation. Their warm-opener examples are exclamatory praise that our praiseIn and no-slop rules reject.

COPPA and privacy. Photo deliverables can show a child's face or home. OpenMAIC sends image submissions to a vision model (evaluator.ts:349-353). The greeting phase tells the model to use the learner's nickname (instructor.ts:75), and the planner input carries nickname and bio (types.ts:581-587). Default should be photos on device only, nothing from the profile sent, and an owner or counsel decision before any AI feedback on photos.

At-home physical safety: model-written steps could propose heat, sharp tools, chemicals, going outside alone or online sign-ups. That needs a code gate plus a grown-up safety card. OpenMAIC has no such gate (its text-only rule covers missing resources, not safety).

Role-play: the Simulator voices an AI character with emotions and private secrets to a child (simulator-system.md). That is high risk for 'feels like AI' and for safety with under-13s. Keep it behind the multi-agent button, grades 6-9, with grown-up consent and no grading of act goals.

Persistence over-engineering: OpenMAIC's fold, drain and hydration (~1,200 lines plus @openmaic/storage) solves a document-versus-runtime split we don't have. Porting it would duplicate Take/TakeRecord and StoreState sync; a small ProjectRun is enough.

Catalogue compatibility: 238 flat project scenes (some with 6 steps, above the AI schema's maximum of 5) must keep rendering, narrating (narration.tsx:75-79) and passing existing tests while the staged form arrives.
Hardcoded strings: kernel 'ready' text and divider labels in six languages, and a Chinese error at instructor.ts:1664. None of it may come over; everything goes through t() with ES parity.
Help accounting: hints and live tutor turns on code-checked project steps must mark them assisted, or project checks will overstate independent success in the Family view.

read:multiagent.summary:
Map of OpenMAIC's multi-agent classroom (modules/openmaic-classroom, abbreviated OM/) and what an opt-in "classroom mode" behind a button would need in apps/web. I only read code. Nothing was run: upstream has no node_modules and no latency instrumentation (OM/eval/orchestration has quality judges only). The cost and latency figures below are estimates worked out from the code's call structure, the prompt sizes and our price table. None of them were measured.

HOW IT WORKS UPSTREAM. There are two director paths.
(1) The legacy path is OM/app/api/chat/route.ts. It calls lib/orchestration/stateless-generate.ts:392, which runs a LangGraph with the shape START→director→agent_generate→END. Each request runs exactly one director→agent cycle (director-graph.ts:479-496). The browser repeats requests until the director says USER or END, or until there are two empty turns. There is no cap on the number of turns (lib/chat/agent-loop.ts:150-268).
  - With 2 or more agents, the director is a non-streaming model call that returns {"next_agent": id|"USER"|"END"} (director-graph.ts:150-222; director-prompt.ts:216-239; prompt template lib/prompts/templates/director/system.md).
  - With 1 agent, the director is code only: it sends the agent once and then cues the learner (director-graph.ts:115-132).
  - In a discussion's first turn, the trigger agent skips the director call (director-graph.ts:135-148).
  - Each agent call streams a JSON array of text and actions, parsed with partial-json (stateless-generate.ts:136-381; director-graph.ts:313-391). Actions are filtered by role (registry/types.ts:83-95, tool-schemas.ts:16-21).
(2) The Pi path is OM/app/api/chat/pi/route.ts → lib/chat/pi/director-loop.ts. It is on by default (lib/config/feature-flags.ts:99-100; the client switches to it at components/chat/use-chat-sessions.ts:1263).
  - One request runs the whole round on the server. The director is a tool-using agent with read_scene, call_agent, cue_user and close_session.
  - Caps: at most 6 agent turns and 8 actions per agent (pi/config.ts:5-8), and at most 18 director tool calls (director-loop.ts:79).
  - If the director stops without choosing, the learner is cued automatically (director-loop.ts:270-272).

ROSTER AND ROLES.
  - There are six default agents: teacher, assistant, and four students. The class clown persona uses "pop culture references, memes" (registry/store.ts:96-119). The other display names are in Chinese (store.ts:74,98,122,146,170).
  - The teacher persona says "Encourage students by name" (store.ts:59).
  - Each course also gets an LLM-generated roster: at least 2 agents, exactly 1 teacher (app/api/generate/agent-profiles/route.ts:299-313).
  - Speech length targets by role: teacher about 100 characters, assistant about 80, student about 50 (prompt-builder.ts:181-204).
  - A peer-context block stops repeated greetings (summarizers/peer-context.ts:21-31).
  - Other agents' messages are re-labelled as the user's, with the sender's name attached (summarizers/message-converter.ts:49-57). An interrupted message gets a marker (message-converter.ts:96-105).

TURN-TAKING WITH THE LEARNER.
  - Director rule 13 forces the teacher to answer an unanswered learner turn first. It is enforced only in the prompt text (director/system.md:25-34).
  - cue_user ends the client loop (agent-loop.ts:246-249) and the UI shows "Your turn".
  - The learner can interrupt at any point (use-chat-sessions.ts:1408-1475, 1565-1630).
  - Generated slides end with a `discussion` action whose agentId is a student (OM/packages/@openmaic/generation/templates/slide-actions/system.md:97-117; OM/packages/@openmaic/dsl/src/action.ts:196-201).
  - That action shows a ProactiveCard that skips itself after 5 seconds (lib/choreography/timing.ts:31; components/chat/proactive-card.tsx:96-117). "Listen" starts a discussion in which a student agent speaks first, unprompted (prompt-builder.ts:107-113).

UI.
  - components/roundtable/index.tsx (2,201 lines): avatars around a table, speech bubble, "Your turn", thinking state, voice input. It uses framer-motion 52 times, including 20 infinite animations, with no reduced-motion check and no aria-live.
  - components/chat/chat-area.tsx: Lecture and Chat tabs (lines 290-301).
  - components/chat/chat-session.tsx: one bubble per sender.
  - lib/buffer/stream-buffer.ts: reveals text at 30 ms per character (about 33 characters a second, lines 208-209). Q&A and discussion add 1.2 s after text and 0.8 s per action (use-chat-sessions.ts:924).
  - lib/hooks/use-discussion-tts.ts: a separate TTS voice per agent.

COST AND LATENCY PER TURN (estimates).
  - Legacy path, k speakers: k+1 director calls plus k agent calls = 2k+1 model calls, run one after another, over k+1 HTTP requests.
  - Prompt sizes: each agent system prompt is about 32-35 KB, roughly 8-9K tokens. That covers agent-system 7.9 KB, the whiteboard reference snippet 17.4 KB, action descriptions and state. Each director prompt is about 2K tokens.
  - For k=2 at the Sonnet 5.5 list price in our apps/web/src/lib/server/budget.ts:63 ($2 in / $10 out per million tokens): about 24K input and 300 output tokens, roughly $0.05 per learner message without caching. Against the default $1 per learner per day (budget.ts:50) that is about 20 messages a day. If every HTTP request counts as a turn (budget.ts:18), it is about 16 messages a day against the 50-turn cap (budget.ts:49).
  - First word: the director call is not streamed and must finish first, adding a full model round trip. That is about +0.6-1.0 s, over the live tutor spec's 3-9 gate of p50 ≤ 1.6 s (docs/plans/2026-10-07-live-tutor-spec.md:386).
  - Between speakers: the browser waits for the text reveal and the 1.2 s pause before it sends the next request (agent-loop.ts:234-235), then pays another director call and another first-token wait. That is about 2-3 s of silence plus TTS.
  - Pi path, for k=2: about 3-4 director steps plus 2 child calls, with the Pi director prompt re-sent at every step. The first word still waits for the director to emit call_agent.

HOW soloTutor NARROWS IT.
  - Only the Kaizen route sets it (app/kaizen/course/[id]/page.tsx:32 → ClassroomSurface.tsx:64,131 → lib/classroom/load-classroom.ts:196-207 → registry/agent-selection.ts:59-72).
  - It picks the teacher by registry role, never by list position. With no teacher, the selection is empty. isUserSet is always false.

  - A fixed roster in code: the tutor plus at most 2 peers, never generated by a model.
  - Turn order decided in code, with no LLM director: the tutor always speaks first, then at most one peer line, then it is the learner's turn. Peers never talk to each other in rounds.

  - `Beat.who` so recordings and replays keep each speaker.
  - Demo mode keeps working: vetted, code-written peer lines live in apps/web/src/lib/tutor-demo.ts.
  - Labels and accessibility: an "AI classmate" label on every peer bubble, an aria-pressed toggle, the speaker name as text, and aria-live.
  - Rough cost: about +60-150 output tokens per turn when a peer speaks, about $0.001-0.002, plus a cached roster block of about 300 tokens. The tutor's first sound is unchanged.
  - Placement: a new phase after T7, behind a KAIZEN_CLASSROOM flag. It depends on T1 (voice), T2 (Beat and recording), T4 (publicObservation) and T5 (the Board director verbs).
  - Blocked on the owner: peer voices. The live tutor spec has one voice for the whole app (:145) and Turbo allows one registered voice per connection (:273). The owner also needs to decide grades, defaults, consent for under-13s, the peer personas, and whether a peer may voice a deliberate mistake.

PROJECT-BASED LEARNING. OpenMAIC's PBL has its own multi-role chat, separate from lib/orchestration: roles instructor, evaluator, mentor, collaborator and simulator (OM/packages/@openmaic/dsl/src/pbl.ts:6-13), served by OM/app/api/pbl/v2/{instructor,simulator,evaluate}. Its evaluator grades with a model, so it can never stand as proof of a skill. Later, a classroom peer could play the "collaborator" role in our 238 project scenes.

The owner's 'maybe … behind a button' needs an explicit spec amendment, and so far it is only a 'maybe'. Escalate it as D-7. Do not decide it silently.

A faithful port breaks the latency and cost gates. The LLM director adds a full non-streaming round trip before every speaker (director-graph.ts:176-182). Between speakers the browser waits for the text reveal at about 33 characters a second plus a 1.2 s pause before it sends the next request (stream-buffer.ts:208-209; use-chat-sessions.ts:924; agent-loop.ts:234-235). k speakers cost 2k+1 model calls, about $0.05 per learner message uncached at k=2. The 3–9 gate of p50 ≤ 1.6 s (live-tutor-spec.md:386) would fail. These figures are estimates, not measurements.

soloTutor does not hold even upstream. startDiscussion puts the scripted student agentId back into the roster (use-chat-sessions.ts:1951-1958), and that agentId comes from the generator prompt (generation/templates/slide-actions/system.md:115). An empty selection silently becomes the stock 'default-1' teacher (use-chat-sessions.ts:1812-1813). Roster writes widen the selection again (stage.ts:734-737). On the default Pi path the director model still runs for a single agent (feature-flags.ts:99-100; there is no single-agent shortcut in pi/director-loop.ts). Lesson for us: the roster must be a constant the server checks on every request, never a client-side selection.

Names reach the model upstream: director-prompt.ts:61-68, prompt-builder.ts:82-87 ('Address them by name'), pi/prompts.ts:209 and :267, sent from use-chat-sessions.ts:1682-1685, 1877-1880 and 2001-2004. Any persona or prompt text copied from here could carry a name instruction back in. The guard: golden-snapshot the persona constants and add a model-call spy test.

Answer leaks through peers. A 'tries' peer that says a wrong value on an open multiple-choice check rules out an option. Upstream itself treats ruling out options as a leak (state-context.ts:234). Upstream also prints the correct answers after submission (state-context.ts:176-211). Peers must never state a value while a check is open, never give a verdict, and never see a key. Allow deliberate-mistake lines only in concept talk on Talk.

Voice. The live tutor spec builds one voice for the whole app (:145), and Turbo allows one registered voice per connection (:273). Peers need distinct, natural EN/ES voices, which means an audition and possibly a second socket opened ahead of time. Device voices for peers would sound uncanny, which the owner ruled out. This is blocked on the owner and needs a P0 vendor check.

Slop and child safety. Upstream personas include a meme-driven class clown and teacher praise by name (store.ts:59, 96-119), and the generated rosters come from a model (agent-profiles route). AI peers that present as children raise parasocial and COPPA-perception concerns. Every peer must carry an 'AI classmate' label, use reviewed personas, and pass praiseIn and greeting checks. Turning it on for under-13s probably needs a grown-up's consent, which is an owner decision.

Accessibility debt if the UI is copied. The roundtable has 20 infinite framer-motion animations, no reduced-motion handling and no aria-live (components/roundtable/index.tsx). ProactiveCard dismisses itself after 5 s (timing.ts:31). The UI has to be rebuilt in our Talk bubbles with text speaker labels.

Budget accounting. If classroom mode ever makes several requests per learner message, the way the upstream client loop does, each one counts as a turn against the 50-a-day cap (budget.ts:18, :49). Keep it to one request.

Model plumbing contamination. Both director paths reach the forbidden lib/ai/llm.ts (ai-sdk-adapter.ts:15; lib/agent/runtime/stream-fn.ts:37), and the chat route runs without screen(), a rate limit or a spend gate (app/api/chat/route.ts:46-92). Port patterns only. check-forbidden and the ESLint ban (theater spec §5.4) must land first.

Unverified upstream behaviour. Its tests and evals were not run (there are no node_modules), and nothing in the repo instruments latency. Every number here is derived from the code and has to be re-measured behind our own tests and evals.

read:html.summary:
Bottom line: OpenMAIC's interactive branch is a good teaching generator inside a weak container. The prompts and the observation contract are worth porting. The live host is not safe for children as written, and it fails our 320 px and keyboard rules. "Take the html" can ship only behind a new host we write ourselves: null-origin, no network, no popups or forms, responsive, in-flow, with gates in code. The HTML may teach and let learners explore. It never grades.

HOW IT WORKS
1. Outline. Interactive Mode (`app/page.tsx:598-602`, toggle `components/generation/interactive-mode-button.tsx`) swaps in `lib/prompts/templates/interactive-outlines/*`, which prefers widgets: about 70% interactive, at least 2 simulations, at least 1 game (`user.md:42-55`). The route is `app/api/generate/scene-outlines-stream/route.ts:430-463`. The parked Kaizen adapter forces `interactiveMode: true` and strips the nickname (`lib/kaizen/client/course-request.ts:141-149`).
2. Content. `generateSceneContent` sends every interactive outline to `generateWidgetContent` (`packages/@openmaic/generation/src/scene-generator.ts:256-281`, `1204-1356`). That picks one of six prompts: simulation, diagram, code, game, visualization3d, procedural-skill (the last only when vocational mode is on, `outline-generator.ts:208-236`). It makes one free-text model call (`:1329`), takes the first `<!DOCTYPE` through the last `</html>` (`:1163-1197`), compile-checks classic inline scripts (`interactive-script-validator.ts:145-156`, `node:vm` compile-only, never run), reads `<script type=application/json id=widget-config>` (`:1361-1379`), and runs `postProcessInteractiveHtml`, which converts LaTeX and injects KaTeX from jsdelivr with `trust:true` (`interactive-post-processor.ts:71-86`).
3. Script. `generateSceneActions`, interactive branch (`:1785-1825`): an element inventory parsed from the HTML (`:1386-1488`, caps of 60 ids, 30 classes, 30 data attributes, 120 chars per value) feeds the interactive-actions prompt. That prompt returns speech plus four verbs, `widget_highlight/setState/annotation/reveal` (`templates/interactive-actions/system.md:59-88`). The parser keeps only those verbs (`action-parser.ts:148-159`), but never checks selectors or state keys against the inventory or config.

HOW THE APP HOSTS IT
- A placeholder (`components/scene-renderers/interactive-renderer.tsx`) registers the HTML in an LRU pool of 3 (`lib/store/interactive-iframe-pool.ts:27`, `120-154`).
- `InteractiveIframeHost` portals the iframes to `document.body`, `position:fixed` over the slot, scaled down from a fixed 1280×720 page (`InteractiveIframeHost.tsx:178-195`, `424-452`; `lib/interactive/logical-viewport.ts:4-28`).
- The sandbox is `allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups`, with no `allow-same-origin` (`:451`, rationale `:215-225`, test `tests/security/iframe-sandbox.test.ts`).
- There is no CSP on the frame. The app header sets only `frame-ancestors` (`next.config.ts:62-78`).
- The host injects four shims before the page: error capture with a buffer it can replay, in-memory localStorage, an element picker, and the observation responder (`lib/utils/iframe.ts:24-110`, `390-411`).

TEACHER INTO THE PAGE
1. `ActionEngine` maps the four verbs to `HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT`, `SET_WIDGET_STATE`, `ANNOTATE_ELEMENT` and `REVEAL_ELEMENT` and waits 300 ms each (`lib/action/engine.ts:275-283`, `862-901`; `lib/choreography/timing.ts:58`).
2. The send callback is looked up per scene at send time (`components/edit/PlaybackChromeRoot.tsx:769-783`). Messages queue until the iframe's `load` (`lib/store/widget-iframe.ts:114-148`), then go by `postMessage(..., '*')` (`Host:314-319`).
3. The page's own listener does the work. It is model-written from a template that runs `querySelector(target)` and never checks `event.source` (`templates/simulation-content/system.md:32-101`).

LEARNER OUT OF THE PAGE
- No event stream comes out, and no verdicts. procedural-skill even forbids `window.parent.postMessage` (`system.md:253`).
- What does come out:
  - runtime errors (`iframe.ts:66-110`, matched on `e.source`, `Host:350-381`), shown raw to the learner (`InteractiveRuntimeErrorBanner.tsx:34-36`);
  - picker picks (Pro mode only);
  - the observation contract. The page publishes an inert `<script type=application/json data-maic-observation>` inside `#experiment` (`snippets/interactive-observation.md`). The host reads it on demand, with identity checks (scene, scope, document and instance ids), an 800 ms timeout, a 32 KB cap, depth ≤ 64, and frozen results (`lib/interactive/observation-bridge.ts:35-224`, `observation.ts:4-95`). The chat route frames it for the model as untrusted evidence (`lib/chat/pi/interactive-state-evidence.ts:162`, `200-243`). The whole path is behind a flag that is off by default (`chat-observation.ts:30`, `feature-flags.ts:107-109`).

FAILURE HANDLING
- Bad HTML, or a classic script that won't parse, gives `onFailure('invalid-model-output')`, then a 500 from the route (`app/api/generate/scene-content/route.ts:346-354`), then the client marks the scene failed and pauses the batch (`lib/hooks/use-scene-generator.ts:869-887`). There is no repair call and no stand-in scene.
- If the script call fails, the fallback narration is in Chinese (`scene-generator.ts:2019-2028`).
- There is no size cap anywhere on generated HTML: `maxOutputTokens` is the whole output window (`route.ts:154`, `169`; DSL `validate.ts:188-198`).

WHAT MAKES IT GOOD (keep)
- Craft rules in the prompts:
  - reset returns to the exact start;
  - an explicit running / paused / ended state;
  - a fair start (no instant fail);
  - controls never cover the canvas;
  - 44 px targets, keyboard shortcuts, presets;
  - procedural-skill: Done can't be the only interaction, wrong choices show consequences, retry without a full reset;
  - game: you learn by doing it, not by answering.
- The observation contract, which is close to our `publicObservation` and `onState`.
- The inventory-first selector rule, with attribute values cleaned so a label can't forge prompt lines (`:1496-1502`).
- parse5 plus a compile-only syntax gate.
- Messages queued until load.
- Error buffer and replay.
- The null-origin rationale and its test.
- The offline packager used by video export (`lib/video-export-app/prepare-interactive-html.ts:30-35`, `211-285`): it inlines remote assets, rejects any URL it can't inline, injects `<meta CSP default-src 'none'; connect-src 'none'; frame-src 'none'; worker-src 'none'…>` first in `<head>`, caps size and hashes the result. That is the right shape for our host.

WHAT IS UNSAFE FOR CHILDREN, OR BREAKS OUR RULES
1. The network is open. Pages and the KaTeX injection pull from cdn.tailwindcss.com, unpkg (Three), jsdelivr (KaTeX), Pyodide, CodeMirror and Monaco. They can also fetch or beacon anywhere, which sends a child's IP and user agent to third parties (COPPA) and opens a supply-chain risk.
2. With `allow-popups` and `allow-forms`, a page can open any website or submit a form off-site. A page can also navigate its own frame to any URL (the sandbox doesn't stop that), and the host keeps posting to whatever loaded. The `url` field loads any external page directly (`interactive-renderer.tsx:39`, `Host:448`).
3. Validation only proves that the scripts parse. It never runs `screen()`, `suitable()`, a language check, a praise check, or a reading-level, alt-text or reduced-motion check. Module scripts, meaning every 3D widget, are skipped entirely (`validator:117-120`).
4. Model-written grading:
   - the code widget embeds `testCases` and `solution` in the page and shows pass or fail (`code-content/system.md:13-25`);
   - games add scores, emoji achievements, time bonuses and high scores (`game-content/system.md:99-117`, `273-281`);
   - `widgetConfig`, solution included, is sent to the script model (`scene-generator.ts:1801`), so a key reaches a prompt;
   - `widget_setState` and `widget_reveal` can show the answer state.
5. Accessibility:
   - at 320 px the 1280×720 scale is 0.25, so 16 px text renders at 4 px and 44 px targets at 11 px;
   - the page's own mobile CSS never applies, because the frame is always 1280 CSS px wide;
   - the frame sits at the end of `<body>` and the placeholder is `aria-hidden`, so focus order and reading order are wrong;
   - the frame title is English and contains the id (`Host:450`);
   - no template mentions reduced motion, and they ask for "OBVIOUS" animation and an infinite pulse (`simulation-content/system.md:63`, `206-217`);

read:html.contracts:
Proposed contracts for our port. Theirs are cited so each change is visible.

1. SCENE TYPE (lib/types.ts)
   ExploreScene = { id; kind: "explore"; title; prompt; html: string /*packed, ≤400 KB*/; hash: string /*sha256 = spotsVersion*/; kind2: "sim"|"diagram"|"steps"|"challenge"; config: { vars: {name,label,min,max,step,start,unit?}[]; reveal?: string[]; spots: {id,label}[] }; describe: string /*code-built text equivalent*/; by: "ai"|"people"; script?: Script }.
   - Label: "Written by AI · for exploring, not counted".
   - It is never a check scene. Proof stays with widget check(), the quiz index, practice check or spoken.ts (AGENTS.md #8).

2. FRAME (ours, replacing InteractiveIframeHost.tsx:437-452)
   <iframe srcdoc={html} sandbox="allow-scripts" allow="" referrerpolicy="no-referrer" title={t("stage.explore.frame",{title})} loading="lazy">.
   - It sits in-flow inside the scene, never portaled, at the slot's real CSS width (no 1280×720 scale).
   - Height comes from the shim's {k:"size",h} message, clamped to 240–1600.
   - A second `load` event (self-navigation) unmounts the frame and shows the fallback.
   - Beside it: a visible text equivalent (`describe` plus the current observation summary) and a "Skip this activity" control.
   - Bans: allow-same-origin, allow-popups, allow-forms, allow-modals, allow-top-navigation, allow-downloads.

3. PACKING (server, modeled on prepare-interactive-html.ts:35)
   The first node in <head> is:
   <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data: blob:; font-src data:; media-src data: blob:; connect-src 'none'; frame-src 'none'; worker-src 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'">.
   - Then the error shim, storage shim and bridge shim (from iframe.ts:24-110, rewritten), then the authored HTML.
   - Math is rendered on the server (no KaTeX script).
   - `<html lang>` is set by code from the locale.
   - Their packager omits form-action; ours adds it.
   - `'unsafe-eval'` is dropped unless a later kind proves it needs it.

4. BRIDGE PROTOCOL (all messages are {v:1, doc:<uuid per pack>, ...})
   - Every handler checks event.source (the shim: === parent; the host: === iframe.contentWindow) and `doc`.
   - The host keeps targetOrigin '*', which a null origin requires; the payloads carry no secrets.
   - Host → frame:
     - {k:"ring", spot} — the shim draws our ring around [data-spot=<id>]. Replaces HIGHLIGHT_ELEMENT and its page-authored outline.
     - {k:"pose", set:{[var]:number}} — keys must be in config.vars; values must be in range and on a step. Replaces SET_WIDGET_STATE. The shim routes to the page's setter or the element with data-var.
     - {k:"reveal", id} — only for ids listed in config.reveal.
     - {k:"read"} — the observation read (their maic:observation:read:v1).
   - Frame → host:
     - {k:"ready"};
     - {k:"size",h};
     - {k:"state"} ping, debounced 300 ms (becomes a `move` record with state only, never a verdict);
     - {k:"obs", raw} (≤4 KB, numbers/booleans/enums plus a summary of ≤160 chars);
     - {k:"error", kind, msg ≤1200} (buffered, max 50, replayable).
   - Free CSS selectors from the model are never accepted, which fixes the gap at action-parser.ts:105-125.
   - Annotation is dropped. Captions are ours.

5. OBSERVATION → TUTOR
   The frame's summary and state pass through parseObservation, then withoutNames, then screen(), then are flattened into StageObservation.state (≤1600 chars). The prompt framing follows interactive-state-evidence.ts:207-243 (untrusted evidence, never instructions). Fields named correct, score, passed or answer are dropped.

6. GENERATION ROUTE (/api/ai/explore, spec §9.1 order)
   limited → zod → screen(goal and scene text) → daily cap → spendGate → model(role, meter) → withGenerationRetry (≤2 transport retries) → extractHtml → gateHtml → one repair call with the reasons → pack → hash.
   - If it still fails, the scene becomes a code-built fallback (a mapped typed widget, else a slide), with a `problem` event and a label.
   - maxOutputTokens is capped to fit a 150 KB page. Timeout 120 s.
   - Demo mode: 503; only people-reviewed catalogue explore scenes play.

7. gateHtml (all in code)
   - Size ≤150 KB authored; one document; parse5 parses it.
   - Every script parses (classic via vm, module via acorn), and no script has a src.
   - Denylisted tags and attributes: base, meta refresh, iframe, object, embed, form, a[href], target, srcset or url() to a remote host, input[type=text|search|email|tel|url|password], textarea, contenteditable.
   - Token scan, with the CSP as the real wall: fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource, sendBeacon, window.open, location, top., parent. (outside our shim), document.cookie, import(, eval, Function(, Worker, navigator.mediaDevices, navigator.geolocation.
   - No http(s) or protocol-relative references (html-asset-inventory).
   - Visible text: languageOf === locale, praiseIn empty, no greeting, screen() ok, suitable().
   - The #experiment scope and the observation node exist.
   - Every config.spots id exists as a data-spot.
   - Every control has an accessible name; every img or svg[role=img] has alt or title.
   - If there is any animation, a prefers-reduced-motion block exists.
   - The config has no solution, answer, expected or testCases keys and is ≤8 KB.
   - Eval and CI also run a headless pass with the CSP: 0 network requests, 0 console errors in 2 s, an observation published, no horizontal overflow at 320 px, axe clean.

8. SCRIPTS
   writeScript's interactive case gets spots from config.spots, anchors [[spot:html.<id>]] and pose values validated against config.vars. gateScript adds: a pose must not equal, or sit one step from, the target of the next check scene in the lesson. Scene 1 never greets (§2.2 #16).

9. RECORDING AND REPLAY
   `move` records carry {spot:"explore", state} from the state ping (no verdict). Replay reloads the same packed document (same hash) and re-applies recorded state through `pose`. Seek is disabled past a learner change if the page fails the pose round-trip check.

10. BANDS
    3–9 first. K–2 explore scenes only with tap-only controls (≤3) and 56 px targets, after the dogfood pass.

11. LICENCE
    Every adapted file carries the §5.1 THU-MAIC MIT header and is listed in apps/web/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. No @openmaic or modules/ imports (check-forbidden).
risks: Spec conflict, not just a port: the owner's 'take the html' reverses tutor-theater §3 D-1 (line 138), §0.6 (37), §5.3 (343, 347-348, 351), §11 (815) and invariant 13.10 (863), plus one-workspace §6 ('the model cannot run JavaScript…') and §7 ('arbitrary generated interactive code' is future work). Escalate and record the owner's words. Don't silently edit the invariants.

Network wall: srcdoc frames inherit the parent's CSP, and apps/web sets none. If the packed meta CSP is ever missing, misplaced (it must come before any script) or stripped by a later rewrite, generated JS can reach any host: child IP and user agent go to third parties (COPPA), and arbitrary code can load. Needs a test that every stored ExploreScene.html starts with the CSP meta, plus re-packing on the server for anything a client posts.

CSP does not govern navigation: a page can still set location to an external site inside its own frame, and the sandbox allows that. Counting a second `load` event and unmounting is the only runtime defence; the gate's location/window.open scan is a second layer. A page that asks the child to type something and then navigates would leak it, which is why free-text inputs are banned in pages.

Model-written grading leaks into proof: games, code and procedural-skill pages compute right/wrong in model JS. Any path that turns the frame's state into an Attempt, a verdict on a `move`, mastery or 'help' accounting breaks AGENTS.md #8. Fields named correct/score/passed must be dropped at the bridge, and the not-counted label must always be visible.

Answer leaks through narration or poses: upstream sends widgetConfig, solution included, into the script prompt (scene-generator.ts:1801), and widget_setState/reveal can display the answer. Strip keys from the config at the gate, and add the gateScript pose-vs-next-check rule.

Accessibility regressions: upstream's 1280×720 scale and body-portal fail 320 px, 44/56 px targets, focus order and screen readers outright. Generated pages are also unreliable on reduced motion, alt text and keyboard parity even with prompt rules, so the headless axe/320 px eval must gate any prompt change, and the text equivalent must carry the lesson on its own.

Quality and latency: one free-text HTML call for a 30–150 KB page is slow (upstream allows 300 s) and often fails the gates. The repair call doubles the cost. Generation must stay in the background with a code fallback ready, and the T7 tap-to-Ready p50 ≤ 45 s bar will likely need explore scenes to arrive after scene 1.
Validator gap: upstream skips module scripts, so every 3D widget is unchecked. Self-hosting Three costs about 600 KB per scene and fights the size cap. Keep visualization3d out of the first cut.

Prompt heritage: Chinese UI examples, first-page greetings, 'OBVIOUS' animation, achievements and emoji, Tailwind CDN, and a forced 70% interactive quota. Each needs rewriting under golden tests. praiseIn, languageOf and the greeting check have to run on the page's visible text, not just on narration.

Privacy through observation: page-reported state goes to the tutor model verbatim upstream. Without withoutNames + screen() + a numbers/enums-only rule, any learner-typed text inside a page (or a malicious imported page) is a name-leak and prompt-injection channel.

Untrusted HTML at rest: upstream renders imported classroom JSON HTML as-is, and the `url` fallback loads any external page. Never accept explore HTML from the client without re-running gateHtml and packing on the server, and never port the `url` field.

Scope: the owner also asked for project-based learning (upstream `pbl/*`, also on spec §5.3's never list, line 347) and the multi-agent classroom behind a button. Those are separate mappings. Explore scenes should fit the existing ProjectScene (apps/web/src/lib/types.ts:127) as its investigate step rather than spawn a second project model.
Upstream tests were not run here (no node_modules, spec §1.8). Port the validator, inventory and observation behaviour behind our own vitest cases, not on trust.
